headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/execute in shared VS Code files while Opik has broad network egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP, so it may ingest content from Opik outputs if those are placed in the shared workspace. Opik has broad network egress and REST API access, but no direct shared channel is documented. The interaction is plausible via files, not proven.
conditions: IF Opik output is saved into the shared VS Code workspace and Roo Code opens or parses it as instructions, prompt injection is possible.
IF an MCP server or file bridge passes Opik-generated text into Roo Code without provenance checks, instruction hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Keep Opik outputs out of the shared workspace.
Require explicit human review before Roo Code reads any Opik-generated file.
Disable or restrict MCP servers that ingest untrusted text.
Use separate directories for agent handoff artifacts.
Add provenance labels to any transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, capture screens, and send data to configured model APIs or MCP servers; Opik has broad network egress and REST API access. If sensitive source code or screenshots enter the shared workspace, Roo Code may transmit them onward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workspace-sharing setups.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared VS Code workspace, Roo Code can read them and forward them to configured APIs or MCP servers.
IF Opik-generated artifacts containing secrets are written into the workspace, Roo Code may ingest and retransmit them.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Turn off screen capture when sensitive material is visible.
Restrict Roo Code model/API endpoints to approved destinations.
Use a separate workspace for agent handoff files.
Scan workspace artifacts for secrets before opening them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and spawn_subprocesses in a workspace-scoped concurrency model shared via filesystem. Opik is not shown to write files, but it has broad network egress and REST API access, so if it also writes artifacts into the same workspace through its API-driven workflow, conflicts can corrupt files or git state. Uncertainty about Opik's write path escalates the risk.
conditions: IF Opik writes artifacts into the same VS Code workspace that Roo Code edits, concurrent writes can collide.
IF both agents touch the same git branch or files without locking, Roo Code can overwrite Opik-produced state.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Use file locks for any shared artifacts.
Review git diffs before committing.
Move Opik outputs to a read-only handoff folder.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and execute shell or git actions with approval, so if it consumes Opik-generated outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or commits. Opik's REST/API-driven outputs may be treated as facts, but no verification loop is documented between the pair. The pathway exists, though not as an automatic default.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Opik output as a source of truth without independent verification, incorrect facts can propagate into edits or commits.
IF Opik produces malformed guidance and Roo Code executes follow-on shell or git actions, the error can cascade.
mitigations: Require a verification step before Roo Code acts on Opik output.
Ask Roo Code to cite source files before editing.
Limit shell and git actions to reviewed changes.
Use a second pass to validate generated facts.
Keep Opik outputs advisory rather than authoritative.

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while Opik is an observability/evaluation tool with broad network egress. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a modest compliance gap is visible: sensitive code or screenshots may flow into a third-party API path. The other agent is not cited beyond its network/API surfaces because no separate compliance regime is stated.
conditions: IF browser screenshots or source code are processed by Roo Code through a non-approved external model API, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF Opik receives regulated data through its REST/API workflow, retention or residency controls may need review.
mitigations: Restrict regulated data from the workspace.
Use approved model endpoints only.
Disable screenshot capture on sensitive tasks.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Document data-flow boundaries before use.
